source_repo_note: The DMTAP specification repository. Renamed from 'dmtap' to 'kotva'; the drift guard's search is name-independent BECAUSE of that rename, and treats a spec-shaped sibling under an unexpected name as a hard failure rather than a skip.
source_commit_subject: core/pubobj: derive announce_id from the signature-EXCLUDED body (§22.3.1/§1.3)
vendored_by: cp, verbatim. This file is INPUT to packages/kerf-pub/tests/test_conformance_vectors.py: never edited in place, never regenerated inside kerf.

supersedes.why: Vendored under the withdrawn §22.3.1 formula announce_id = 0x1e || BLAKE3-256(det_cbor(PubAnnounce)) over the COMPLETE signed object. §1.3 forbids deriving an identifier from a signature and §18.1.6 concedes hybrid AND-composition is EUF-CMA and not SUF-CMA, so that formula let one semantic announce carry two announce_ids. The spec corrected it to exclude key 9 (sig) and regenerated the corpus; every announce_id, dependent supersedes reference, feed-entry id and feed-head tip/sig moved. kerf-pub's PubAnnounce.id was corrected to match in the same change.
supersedes.undetected_because: The drift guard searched for the spec repo under its pre-rename name 'dmtap' and therefore skipped on every machine, including ones with the spec checked out.

how_to_resync: Re-run the suite: a drift that is a protocol correction will fail the replay tests too, and kerf-pub's own code must then follow the spec.
